criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), identified users (marine/conservation scientists), strong justification with statistics and four cited sources, plus an innovative sensing concept (seafloor colour change). Falls short of full marks because no quantified mission requirements (resolution, revisit, coverage, payload) or objectives are stated.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
In 2016, a bleaching killed 30 percent of the reef’s coral. In 2017, another 20 percent perished.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A reasonably detailed Gantt chart and task-by-task descriptions covering launch, orbit, comms, EOL and STK give confidence the project is feasible. However, no contingencies or schedule slack/variation provision are given, and the link to the mission concept is only implicit, so it sits at the top of Adequate.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.
**Strategies:** The goal is to brainstorm and research as many possible strategies for the satellite’s launch/orbit

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Only background reading and completion of four STK tutorials is reported; no design results, calculations, orbit/launch analysis or sensor trades are presented. This is minor work with no interpretation of results, matching the top of the Adequate band rather than Deficient, since a foundation has been laid.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Well written, logical headings, clear prose and a legible, labelled Gantt chart; numbered footnotes match the reference list. Mark reduced because the source list is a raw 'Useful Links' block of bare URLs rather than a consistently formatted reference list, and the Gantt colour legend (gold/blue) does not match the chart shown.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.

technical_issues.issue: No quantified mission requirements: spatial resolution, spectral bands, revisit time, coverage, data rate or mission lifetime are never specified, so the concept is not yet designable.
No orbit, altitude, launch vehicle or payload sizing analysis; COEs/AOEs and launch specifics are only listed as future tasks, so space-segment feasibility is unsubstantiated.

Gantt legend states completed stages are gold and incomplete blue, but completed cells appear yellow; the red deadline line placement and Week 9 finish for STK design are inconsistent with the Week 10 finalisation note.
References given as bare URLs without titles, authors or dates; in-text footnote numbering does not map to a single consistent reference list.

overall: Attractive, well-written mission concept with a sound rationale and a plausible Gantt plan, but no quantitative requirements or real design analysis yet. Presentation is strong; references need formatting. Progress is essentially background research plus STK tutorials, so the technical evidence lags the narrative.

feedback.summary: You present an attractive, well-written GBR bleaching-monitoring concept with clear users and strong justification, plus a plausible Gantt plan. The main gap is quantitative mission requirements and real design analysis: progress is background research and STK tutorials. References need consistent formatting, and the Gantt legend should match the chart. Build on this strong narrative by adding numbers, contingencies and preliminary technical results.
next_steps: Quantify the mission: add spatial resolution, spectral bands, revisit time, coverage, data rate and mission lifetime to Mission Concept & Rationale, and tie each to user needs.

Strengthen Project Plan & Preliminary Progress: add schedule slack/contingencies and explain explicitly how each task follows from the mission concept; then produce preliminary orbit/payload/launch sizing results with brief interpretation.

Tidy presentation: replace Useful Links bare URLs with a consistent reference list (titles, authors, dates) and correct the Image 1 Gantt legend/deadline so it matches the chart and Week 10 finalisation.

criteria.C1: Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly identifies GBR bleaching monitoring, marine/conservation scientists as users, and justifies need with statistics and four sources; the seafloor colour-change sensing idea is innovative. To reach full Accomplished, specify quantified mission requirements—spatial resolution, spectral bands, revisit time, coverage, data rate and lifetime—and state explicit objectives so the concept is designable.
criteria.C2: Your Project Plan & Preliminary Progress includes a detailed Gantt chart and task descriptions for launch, orbit, comms, EOL and STK, which makes the project believable. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, add contingencies and schedule slack/variation provision, and make explicit why the plan is structured this way for your mission concept; include appropriate source references.
criteria.C3: You report background reading on Asner’s Hawaii system and coral bleaching, and completion of STK tutorials 1–4; this is a useful foundation. To raise Preliminary Progress, present actual preliminary design results—orbit/altitude, launch vehicle, payload/sensor sizing or trades—with brief description and interpretation, so you are clearly on track for completion.
criteria.C4: Your report is well written with logical headings, clear prose and a labelled Gantt chart; numbered footnotes match the reference list. To reach full Accomplished, replace the Useful Links bare URLs with a consistent reference list (titles, authors, dates) and correct the Image 1 Gantt legend/deadline so completed stages and Week 9/Week 10 timing match the chart.
